description:
FILED s428 (Fable), found by the s427 review probes of the readline/glob
whitelist.  PRE-EXISTING: byte-identical emission on main before s427 (A/B'd
on ff0cd86 vs the merged tree), so s427's whitelist (which correctly classes
`<main::FH2>` as a readline — perl reads a line) did not change it.

    open(main::FH2, '<', $file) or die;
    my $l = <main::FH2>;          # perl: a line   PCL: "The variable FH2 is unbound" at LOAD
    $l = readline(main::FH3);     # perl: a line   PCL: a line   — emits (p-readline 'main::FH3)

Emission (same on both trees):
    (p-my-= $l (p-scalar-ctx (p-readline main::FH2)))    <- bare symbol, read in package main as FH2
    (p-my-= $l (p-readline 'main::FH3))                  <- the readline() builtin path, quoted

So the `<…>` readline node's bareword-handle leaf (Pl/PExpr.pm parse(), the
`readline` node built right after the whitelist test) emits a qualified
handle name as a bare symbol where the unqualified `<FH>` goes through the
filehandle-name mangler (`|fh|`, matching what `open(FH …)` declared) and the
`readline(PKG::FH)` builtin quotes it.  Reuse rule (CLAUDE.md §11): route the
qualified spelling through the SAME handle-name path `<FH>` and
`readline(PKG::FH)` use; do not add a branch.  The crash is LOUD (unbound
variable at load) but it kills the whole FILE.

Corpus: 0 rows in perl-tests/ carry `<main::` / `<STDIN` qualified (grep -a);
check perl's t/io before fixing — `<main::STDIN>`-style spellings may sit
there.  Guard: a row in Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t's glob/readline section
(or misc-fixes-02.t — NO, that file is closed by size; use -01 above).


=== s438g (Opus 5, 2026-08-23) DONE, by the reuse route this task named: ONE
predicate widened, not a branch added.

`Pl::ExprToCL::_bareword_fh_p` tested a PLAIN identifier
(`/^[^\W\d]\w*$/`), so `main::FH2` failed it and the token was passed through
UNQUOTED -- `(p-readline main::FH2)`, a bare CL symbol that died at LOAD with
"The variable FH2 is unbound" and took the whole file with it.  The predicate
now accepts a package-qualified name.

THE SAME PREDICATE SERVES TWO SITES, and both were broken the same way -- this
is the rule-11 payoff: `<main::FH2>` (gen_readline_form) AND
`print main::FH5 "x"` (gen_filehandle_form's `:fh` marker) both died at load,
while `readline(main::FH3)` was always right because the BUILTIN path quotes
the name itself.  One spelling of one thing, answered three ways by two
predicates and a builtin; now two of the three agree by construction.

MEASURED: corpus-diff 1 of 111 files differ -- `perl-tests/method.t`, ONE hunk,
line 672's `while (<Colour::H1>)`, exactly the shape (the file is PARTIAL at
test 124 for an unrelated reason, so no row moves yet; the landmine is gone).
emission-ab over the four populations: 951 files, SAME 950 / DIFF 1 / RCDIFF 0
-- the one DIFF is `t/op/method.t`, the companion twin of the same statement.
Full sweep TOTAL 18312 (+0), 0 new / 0 fixed, drops 5 = census, GATE clean.
Gate 166/5775.  Guard: four rows in Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t (13 -> 17) --
two positives and two INVERSES (a lexical `$fh` is a form to evaluate and must
never be quoted; an unqualified bareword is unchanged); inverse-guarded on a
cf0076c worktree, where rows 14-15 fail and 16-17 pass.

NOTE for whoever writes the next guard here: `print NAME LIST` is only a
filehandle print when the file has DECLARED NAME as a handle, so the row needs
its `open` -- without it the same text is a call to a sub of that name, which
is perl's reading too.
title: `<PKG::NAME>` — a package-QUALIFIED bareword filehandle inside angle brackets emits an UNBOUND CL symbol `(p-readline main::FH2)`; `readline(main::FH2)` quotes it correctly
